provider.name: GitHub
provider.description: GitHub is a code hosting platform for version control and collaboration, offering Git-based repository management, issue tracking, and continuous integration features.

authMethod.text: GitHub OAuth apps use standard OAuth 2.0 for authorization and authentication.
authMethod.quote: Both OAuth apps and GitHub Apps use OAuth 2.0.

difficulty.rationale: GitHub OAuth app registration requires no mandatory approval or external review process before launch.

handsOnEffort.basis: Assumes creating an app in GitHub Developer Settings and copying credentials into Composio.

summary.text: GitHub does not require external app review or verification to create and use an OAuth app.

publishedTimeline.text: GitHub publishes no timeline because no external app review process is required for OAuth apps.

prerequisites.text: A personal GitHub account or administrative access to a GitHub organization.
prerequisites.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

redirectRules.text: GitHub allows specifying up to 10 authorization callback URLs for an OAuth app.
redirectRules.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

model.text: Scopes specify exact permission access requested during authorization.
model.quote: Scopes let you specify exactly what type of access you need.

examples.grants: Grants full access to public and private repositories including read and write access to code, commit statuses, repository invitations, collaborators, deployment statuses, and repository webhooks.
Grants access to read a user's profile data.
Grants read access to a user's email addresses.

steps.title: Evaluate Managed vs Custom Auth
steps.action: Decide whether to use Composio Managed Auth or register a custom OAuth app.
steps.actorReason: An agent can check whether managed auth or custom credentials fit your branding and scope requirements.
steps.text: Composio provides managed OAuth for GitHub by default, but custom configs can be created for custom branding or specific scopes.
steps.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit.

steps.title: Navigate to Developer Settings
steps.action: Open GitHub Settings and select Developer settings -> OAuth apps.
steps.actorReason: Requires logged-in interaction within the developer's GitHub account.
steps.text: From GitHub profile settings, open Developer settings in the left sidebar and select OAuth apps.
steps.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings.

steps.title: Register New OAuth Application
steps.action: Click 'New OAuth App' and fill in Application Name and Homepage URL.
steps.actorReason: Requires entering app details in the user's GitHub developer portal.
steps.text: Enter the public application name and full website homepage URL.
steps.quote: In Application name, type the name of your app.

steps.title: Set Authorization Callback URL
steps.action: Copy Composio redirect URI and paste into Authorization callback URL.
steps.where: GitHub New OAuth App form & Composio Dashboard
steps.actorReason: Requires retrieving callback URI from Composio and pasting into GitHub settings.
steps.text: Enter the callback URL provided by Composio into GitHub's Authorization callback URL field.
steps.quote: In Authorization callback URL, type the callback URL of your app.

steps.title: Save Application and Generate Client Secret
steps.action: Click 'Register application' and generate a Client Secret.
steps.actorReason: Generating and viewing secret keys must be performed directly by the account owner.
steps.text: Register the app, copy the Client ID, and generate a new Client Secret.

steps.title: Create Auth Config in Composio
steps.action: Enter Client ID and Client Secret into Composio Auth Config setup.
steps.actorReason: Requires copying secrets from GitHub into the Composio interface.
steps.text: Create a custom auth config for GitHub in Composio and save the credentials.
steps.quote: After you enter the required credentials, click Create and copy the auth config ID

steps.title: Pass Auth Config ID in Code
steps.action: Include the auth config ID in your session configuration.
steps.actorReason: An agent can update project code to include the auth config ID parameter.
steps.text: Pass the generated auth config ID into authConfigs in your Composio session initialization.
steps.quote: A session uses your config only when you pass its ID to authConfigs, keyed by toolkit.

faq.question: Does Composio support GitHub Apps?
faq.answer:
Yes. You can bring your own GitHub App by configuring its client ID and client secret in the GitHub auth config.

The GitHub App installation step is separate from the OAuth credential setup. The user still needs to install the GitHub App on the relevant account or organization and grant repository access before GitHub App based tool calls can work. GitHub App permissions come from the app's GitHub settings and installation grant, not from auth config scopes.
